Full Apogea Map vs Map what was open to players.

**• When next playtest?**
ED: Playtest can be in 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, it depends on when we will finish polishing the map. When we finish openning the map we will work on verticality, more dungeons, more caves, etc. Prefer to take more time to release it, so it doesn't feel like a rushed developed game.

**• When release?**
ED: No objective answer.

**• What about the guild system?**
ED: The current guild system is a  problem. ~ Proceeds to talk about other problems, quoting greefing and bosses loot ~ we have to revisit it, didn't put enough thought on it. Don't want anything too complex. Needs to be more impactful. We don't know how to do that yet.

*-- Ed also commented, on how he dislikes hunting spots, just for the sake of hunting. No story behind it, just an artificial spot for players to hunt. Proceeds to explain the lore behind some hunting spots*

**• What your vision for PVP?**
ED: I don't see pvp as a intrinsic part of the game, it's just part of the game. I don't want it to be thematic. I Don't want it to be a fun event to do, but a justice tool. Something that happens in the game to solve politics issues. Not something to do just because it's fun. Though some cool events may happen, like the last 2 days of the playtest where you didnt lose anything. Not something that you need to engage with to progress. Not gatekeeping any content. Only zone there will be pvp-locked are some Dungeons

**• PVP 1v1 Arena? Garadum Arena?**
ED: I really wanna do that, but i'm scared. I'm scared to go against the essence of Apogea design. Maybe something like that would take off the Weight of PVP as something meant to be taken seriously. We gonna have to think about it

*-- Ed commenting on some quests, such as broadsword being too doable early on. And that he wants to make the early game harder. He also mentioned that he likes that some quests are cheesable, he thinks that's funny to watch*
*-- Ed also commented on how he likes to give freedom to the players regarding itemization, "go bow as a mage, go staff as a knight, i don't care". Also said that he think balancing classes are very doable*

**• What about items?**
ED: I want to create more, so you guys have more choices, more options to create distinct builds. The problem with adding a lot of items is mainly balancing. But i will add a lot more items. *Also mentioned that he doens't really wanna make them appear on the character model, so they dont have to care about Visual progression, maybe later when the company grows*

**• Are we gonna have Tier 3 Outfits on next Playtest? - Cloaks mentioned -**
ED: I don't like the outfit quests the way they are right now, delivering items is crap design. Im gonna change that, Tier 3 will be hard af to get.

*-- Ed commented that next test, he will probably at the end of it, boosts everybody experience so players have a taste of endgame content*

**• What about servers on release?**
ED: Aiming for 1000 players capacity per server, instead of 600 like they were on this test. The problem is the map is not that big yet. Also premium exclusive servers probably will be a thing, so people that really likes the game, can avoid queues. If the demand grows too big we will just open new servers, if there are dead servers we will merge them.

**• How much does a 3 week playtest server cost?**
ED: I don't know, but SA server was the most expensive, and NA servers were the cheaper. It's based on traffic. I don't have the exact numbers

**• Peak number of players?**
ED: 7k Online + 5k on queues so roughly 12k players wanting to play the game.
Past the first days, 3k players was roughly the amount of active players. When announced the end of the playtest, that dropped to 1k.

**• What's the best way to support Apogea?**
ED: patreon, but be aware, i only want you to pay patron if you want to support development, not to expect a reward out of it. There will be few minor rewards, but you should not care for them.

**• Apogea Development Team size?**
ED: 6 people including the musician
*-- Commenting on which dev did what animation/texture in the game and how cool some of them look, MATT mentioned as the main artist.* ** (W MATT)**
*Felipe mentioned as main 3D Model designer.* **(W FELIPE)**
*Ed mentioned himself, as the main lore and the head of the project* **(W ED)**
*Bruno mentioned as the Main back-end developper* **(W BRUNO)**
*Dan mentioned as the server & security related specialist* **(W DAN)**
*Other participations such as voice actors mentioned*

**• How much of the game you think it's already completed? Feb 9th 2026**
ED: Well, i thought it was 70% done, but we developped around 10% more, and i still think we sitting at 70%, so i'm not really sure, but roughly around that. The main part that is missing is the map. We need 1 more starting area, and more dungeons, caves, etc.
*Ed commented that he used 2 of community designed map, one of them being the floating castle, and the other one was the bandit camp that they used as an inspiration to create the bandit port. There are also some other community made maps such as one huge castle that ed thinks it's really cool and will use it somehow in the future.*
*Ed also said that all suggestions need to pass through ED filter, so the game doesn't lose it's essence*

**• What you DON'T want from Tibia inspiration?**
ED: I look alot for the negative sides of those inspirations, and try to avoid them. The game has no loading screens whatsoever. I don't like the afk tibia skill training, tend to avoid those afk grinding mechanics. Tibia kept adding more progression to the game ad infinitum, to addict players with no actual late game, it's just the same grinding over and over, until you are strong enough to be able to kill some harder mob over and over again, like a repetitive cycle.

*Ed proceeds talking about UI/UX, like movement tutorials, mechanic explanations. He said that if he makes the game too smooth, with everything explained, it's too boring. It's more of the same, from what i'ts already in the market.*

**• What do you invision for late game?**
Ed: The way i invision late game is that there is 2 types of economy, experience economy and money economy. I Want to make points of interest, that are pvp-locked, that you need your guild to do it, for a specific reason, that will create a punishing, thrilling end-game. Bosses x Wars x Hunting Spots.

**• What's the expected timeline for player progression?**
ED: The normal timeline for a regular player will be something like: a day to level 10, maybe few hours. Around a week to get level 24, and then level 35 needs to be around 2 weeks to a month. And then for level 50 around 2 months or more. Level 70 around an year to get. And so on. I like how the current progression is.

*Ed commented an anti-account sharing system that will be implemented next playtest*
*he also commented that he wants to change the trait tree system, so more builds comes online earlier, the example he gave was to give the players an extra trait point every 5 levels or something like that. Also a change that you can't have multiple tier 3 traits from the same tree, and finish all the tier 4 traits that the game is lacking in the moment*

**• How long are you guys are working on the game?**
ED: 4 years, but only started with playtests roughly 1 year ago

**• What will be the rewards for the top players from this playtest?**
ED: It will be patreon months for free for the top 5 players of each server.

**• Which class wrote more feedbacks?**
ED: <:knight:1384439084474433600> Knights, you guys are loud

**• What about players discovering things?**
ED: There were some stuff that you guys didn't figure it out. But there were a lot of stuff that i didn't expect people to figure it out so fast

**• What was the most tiring thing about the playtest?**
ED: People tagging me telling me that the game sucks. I don't care about those kind of feedbacks where you propose changes and stuff, but when you tag me to tell me that my game sucks, i don't understand.

**• What do you think the game needs?**
ED: Besides more content, there are a bunch of imperfections on the game, that i really wish we could fix. QOL features, a lot of stuff is lacking. For example the health cast needs a warning.

*Ed commented about balancing, that the game is designed so you have to waste money to do most of the stuff in the game, so the economy doesnt inflates and the server dies*

**• What about professions?**
ED: I can't reward you for standing still doing something that is not a challange. That's why i had a hardtime adding fishing. If those mechanics exist they will be something that's its not very rewardable, with big downtimes and such. Professions should be a tool, to help you complete your challanges.

**• Whats your idea for Blessed Amulets and Late game gold sink?**
ED: I don't really like it the way it is right now, it's both too good and clunky. I will add a blessing that you can buy on churches with priests that protects you and blessed amulets will maybe just prevent item loss... I'm honestly not sure.

**• Stance position on RMT?**
ED: Apogea is not supposed to be around RMT, it will be against the rules. If we catch you, you will be banned. But we don't have a good way to track that

**• Bestiaries/Achievements tracking? **
ED: Later on after the game release

**• Mail System in the game?**
ED: It will be something that will require a quest to do.

**• Throphys? Achievements when you kill bosses?**
ED: I really like that idea, i like titles, like when you click: You see anugy, he is an Orc Slayer kinda thing

**• Mounts?**
ED: I will put a rat shipper mount for 50k dollars just for the meme
ANUGY: i will still buy it

**• Housing System for shared houses**
ED: Maybe. Not a simple system, but it's a good idea, like you can assign rooms to some people. Not a priority right now

**• Furniture?**
ED: Im gonna add a lot of furnitures, house npcs, cats (W ED), dont want to spoiler too much.

**• Repeatable quests?**
ED: There will be a repeatable quest for you to regenarate faith, it's already in the code.

**• Queue priority for premium players?**
ED: Not fair with free account players. If you want lower queues go play premium servers

**• What about the rune system?**
ED: Im not happy about it, no negative effects, everybody was just throwing runes everywhere on the equips

**• PVP Exclusive, Hardcore, PVP-Enforced Server?**
ED: Yes, it's already coded, the problem is demmand. Hardcore server makes your character deletes itself if dies. People need to ask for it otherwise, it will just spread the community too much

**Part 1 Summary: “Talking About Apogea With Ed” (0:00 - ~1:35:00)**
This portion of the discussion is primarily a deep dive into Apogea's development philosophy, launch plans, PvP systems, progression, secrets, itemization, and long-term vision.

__1. PvP Test Results and Server Performance__
Ed considers the recent PvP test a success overall, although it did not fully achieve its goal of stress-testing the servers because fewer players participated than expected.
Key Takeaways:
•    The test confirmed several design theories and technical assumptions.
•    Player participation was lower than expected because: 
o    The test was not heavily advertised.
o    The PvP-focused nature likely discouraged some players.
•    Server performance exceeded expectations.
•    Massive optimization work was completed before the test.
Technical Improvements:
Ed spent roughly six weeks optimizing:
•    Physics systems
•    Movement calculations
•    Server networking
•    Rendering performance
The game can now theoretically handle:
•    ~1,000 players visible on screen
•    Up to 1,500 before major degradation begins
One of the biggest wins was that players reported significantly smoother gameplay than prior tests.

__2. World Expansion and Launch Roadmap__
Ed currently keeps the roadmap mostly in his head.
Pre-Launch Plan
Before launch:
•    Expand all four corners of the map.
•    Open remaining major regions.
•    Add: 
o    Death dungeon
o    War dungeon
o    Additional hunting areas
o    Quests
o    NPCs
o    Loot tables
o    Monsters
He refers to this as "thickening" the world.
The goal is to ensure 1,000 concurrent players have enough content and hunting grounds.
Post-Launch Plan
After launch:
•    Expand beyond current borders.
•    Open previously locked regions.
•    Develop endgame content connected to the "Underworld."
•    Add additional islands and map expansions.
A recently-developed map generation system now allows them to expand the world almost indefinitely.

messages.content:
__3. Content Philosophy__
One of Ed's strongest design beliefs:
Most players never reach extreme endgame levels.
Because of this:
•    He does not want to design content primarily for level 100+ players.
•    Instead, he prefers creating: 
o    New zones
o    New experiences
o    New secrets
o    Horizontal progression
Rather than endless power creep.

__4. Future Updates: Incremental, Not Expansions__
Apogea will likely evolve similarly to previous tests.
Instead of giant expansion packs:
Example Philosophy:
•    Add a city.
•    Rework old quests.
•    Add caves.
•    Improve NPC dialogue.
•    Adjust progression balance.
Ed prefers constantly revisiting and improving existing content rather than dropping huge content dumps.

__5. Launch Success Metrics__
Ed says two things will determine Apogea's future:
*A. Retention*
Question: Do players keep playing?
If retention is low:
•    Development accelerates.
•    Emergency updates happen.
•    More aggressive content patches are pushed.
If retention is high:
•    Development proceeds at a healthier pace.
•    More careful design decisions.
•    Potentially more servers.
________________________________________
*B. Revenue*
Question: Does the game sustain itself financially?
•    Good revenue = more servers and content.
•    Poor revenue = slower growth.
Still, Ed repeatedly emphasizes:
Apogea is primarily a passion project, not a money project.
He states that even if only a handful of players remained, he would likely keep at least one server running.

__6. Steam Reviews and Niche Appeal__
Ed expects launch reviews on Steam to be rough.
His reasoning:
•    People leave negative reviews more often than positive ones.
•    Apogea is intentionally punishing.
•    The game will frustrate many players.
Interestingly:
He sees this as potentially beneficial.
A niche community of dedicated players may be healthier for Apogea than trying to appeal to everyone.

__7. PvP Dungeon Philosophy__
A major discussion centered around PvP dungeons.
Todd raises concerns about:
•    Exit camping
•    Forced PvP builds
•    Players leaving dungeons weakened
Ed's response:
These frustrations are largely intentional.
Core Philosophy:
He wants players to:
•    Fear death
•    Travel carefully
•    Build social networks
•    Bring allies
•    Use alternate characters
This mirrors classic Tibia-style gameplay.
He believes:
•    Conflict creates stories.
•    Friction creates community.
•    High risk creates meaningful decisions.
Without those elements, the world feels artificial.

__8. Seven-Day PvP Flag System__
The new 7-day flag reinforces those goals.
Instead of:
•    Killing someone
•    Instantly clearing your flag
Now:
•    Actions have lasting consequences.
•    Players can retaliate.
•    Rivalries and wars become possible.
Ed views this as critical for long-term player-driven conflict.

__9. Alt Characters Are Important__
Ed repeatedly emphasizes alternate characters.
Their purpose:
•    Reduce frustration.
•    Encourage experimentation.
•    Enable riskier gameplay.
Your "main" character becomes valuable.
Your alt becomes the character you risk.
This mirrors old-school MMORPG behavior patterns.

__10. Blessed Amulets Changes__
One of the more concrete confirmations:
Blessed Amulets Will No Longer Be Purchasable
Instead:
•    They must be earned.
•    They will likely be rare.
•    They become meaningful resources.
The goal is restoring risk to the economy.
Ed disliked how easy access to Amulets trivialized death.

__11. Blood Moon System__
Ed admits Blood Moon is:
"Very gimmicky."
However, he has no plans to change it yet.
Why?
Players still haven't uncovered much of what it does.
Blood Moons Include:
•    Stronger monsters
•    Different monster behavior
•    Different loot tables
•    Hidden secrets
Ed believes players have only scratched the surface.
His stance is:
Leave it alone and let the community discover things naturally.

__12. Item Rarity and Forging__
One of the biggest confirmed design decisions:
Extremely Rare Items WILL NOT Drop With Rarity
Examples:
•    Onyx gear
•    Rare boss equipment
•    Similar chase items
These will always drop as:
•    Common quality
If players want higher quality versions:
They must forge them.
Purpose:
•    Prevent lucky day-one legendaries.
•    Extend progression.
•    Create long-term item goals.

__13. Forging System Details Revealed__
Ed openly reveals forging odds:
Tier    Success Chance
Common → Uncommon    **25%**
Uncommon → Rare    **15%**
Rare → Epic    **5%**
Epic → Legendary    **1%**
Forging-related quests also provide hidden bonuses that can increase success chances.
This surprised many because the mechanic is far more complicated than players realized.

__14. Secret Content and Unique Items__
One of the most exciting sections.
Ed confirms:
Truly Unique Items Exist
Examples:
•    Ring of Fire
•    Golden Button
•    Other secret rewards
Characteristics:
•    Only one player can legitimately obtain them.
•    They are not infinitely farmable.
•    Some are still undiscovered.
Additional Revelations:
The Ring of Fire:
•    Exists.
•    Is obtainable.
•    Can theoretically be earned at level 1.
•    Requires no combat.
Even extensive datamining has failed to reveal how to obtain it because portions of the logic exist entirely server-side.

__15. Quest Design Philosophy__
Ed loves community "zerg" moments.
Examples:
•    Brass Armor rushes
•    Cutlass rushes
•    Swamp Troll raids
•    Terror Spider disasters
He considers these moments part of the intended experience.
His focus isn't necessarily efficiency.
It's creating memorable stories players talk about years later.

__16. Rune System Is in Trouble__
Perhaps the biggest uncertainty discussed:
Ed Does Not Like Current Runes
His criticisms:
•    Not intuitive.
•    Too one-dimensional.
•    Everybody chooses the same runes.
•    They fail to meaningfully alter gameplay.
He seriously considered deleting the system entirely.
However, Todd suggested a different approach:
Runes that:
•    Trade stats
•    Modify builds
•    Create unique class identities
Examples:
•    Fire Mage
•    Paladin-style Mage
•    Berserker Knight
Ed immediately responds positively and says it gives him new ideas for redesigning the system.

**Part 2 Summary: “Talking About Apogea With Ed” (~1:36:00 - End)**
Part 2 shifts from broad game philosophy into progression balance, economy, housing, PvP design, launch readiness, and future development plans. A recurring theme is Ed doubling down on risk, scarcity, and player-driven systems rather than convenience.

__1. Experience Curve and Progression Overhaul__
One of the biggest changes discussed is the complete XP rebalance.
Goals of the XP Changes:
•    Stop players from farming starter mobs forever.
•    Make harder enemies worth the risk.
•    Push players toward progressively harder content.
•    Encourage group hunting.
Examples Given:
Previously:
•    Sunskins
•    Ghosts
•    Ghouls
•    Bandits
often provided better XP/hour than much stronger enemies.
Now:
•    Stronger enemies give substantially more XP.
•    Weaker mobs were heavily nerfed.
Ed specifically wants progression to look like:
Starter mobs → stronger mobs → group content → endgame content
rather than:
Starter mob → starter mob → starter mob for 30 levels.

__2. Early Game XP Boosts__
Ed revealed the current early-level progression bonuses:
Levels    XP Multiplier
1-5    2.5x
5-10    2.0x
10-15    1.5x
15-20    1.25x
20+    Normal XP
This exists to:
•    Speed up awkward early progression.
•    Allow builds to come online sooner.
•    Get players into meaningful content faster.

__3. Extra Skill Points__
Bonus skill points stop at:
Level 15
Players receive bonus points at:
•    Level 5
•    Level 10
•    Level 15
This effectively allows builds to come online roughly 4 levels earlier than before.
__
4. Tier 5 Traits Need More Work__
Ed openly admits some Tier 5 traits are weak.
Examples discussed:
•    Scared Juggler
•    Echoread
•    Several others
His Position:
Not every trait needs to be perfect at launch.
He expects:
•    Meta shifts
•    Player experimentation
•    Unexpected discoveries
Similar to earlier tests where players eventually broke traits that initially looked weak.
He plans to continue improving them post-launch.

__5. Housing Changes__
Several housing updates have already been implemented.
House Depos Removed
You can no longer use houses as mini-depots.
Players must return to towns and depots.
Reason:
•    Encourage travel.
•    Preserve world activity.

__Guild-Like Houses__
Larger houses now support:
•    Multiple ownership rooms.
•    Sub-owners.
•    Shared housing structures.
A master owner can manage the entire property while sub-owners manage individual sections.

__Invite Restrictions__
Players can only be invited to:
3 Houses Maximum
Purpose:
Prevent large guilds from controlling huge portions of the map through housing ownership.

__More Houses Coming__
Ed confirmed:
•    Many more houses are being added.
•    More unique and scenic houses are planned.
•    He particularly loves the "hobbit hole" style houses.

__6. PvP Arenas and Coliseums__
Todd asked about:
•    Arenas
•    Duels
•    Tournaments
•    Safe PvP zones
Surprisingly:
Ed Is Hesitant
His reasoning is interesting.
He believes Apogea PvP is only meaningful because of:
•    Risk
•    Resources
•    Terrain
•    Escape routes
•    Monsters
•    Reputation
•    Travel distance
•    Consequences
A safe arena removes all of those.
He worries:
A coliseum would expose how mechanically simple Apogea's PvP actually is.
In his view:
The depth comes from the world itself, not combat rotations.

__7. Emergent Gameplay Philosophy__
Ed repeatedly emphasizes:
Don't Build Sidewalks
Players create their own stories.
If developers over-design content:
•    Emergent gameplay disappears.
•    Organic interactions disappear.
•    Systems feel artificial.
His goal remains:
Give players tools. Let them create experiences.

__8. Secrets, Books, and Hidden Clues__
Todd asks if books and cryptic lore entries actually matter.
Ed gives a very clear answer:
Yes.
He claims:
•    Nothing is placed randomly.
•    Books can contain clues.
•    Secrets often have breadcrumbs.
•    Some misleading information also exists intentionally.
This section reinforces that Apogea's secrets are often multi-layered and require player investigation.

__9. Health Regeneration Is Still Too Strong__
One of the most surprising statements:
Ed still thinks regeneration is overpowered.
Even after multiple nerfs:
He believes players haven't fully optimized it yet.
Future possibilities:
•    Shorter food durations
•    Reduced regeneration efficiency
•    More weight penalties

__10. Why Regen Is Being Nerfed__
Ed's reasoning ties into the economy.
His desired loop:
Hunt → Spend Resources → Profit Eventually
Not:
Hunt Forever → Infinite Profit
He believes:
If healing becomes free:
•    Food becomes meaningless.
•    Potions lose value.
•    Healers become irrelevant.
•    Economy collapses.

__11. Healers Need to Matter__
A major balance goal:
Make Healing Classes Valuable
Ed wants players to think:
"Great, we have a healer."
Rather than:
"Why bring a healer?"
This is one reason behind:
•    Regen nerfs
•    Stronger content
•    Resource management
He wants group composition to matter.

__12. Economy Philosophy__
This was one of the strongest sections.
Ed wants an economy where:
Loot Matters
When a rare item drops:
Players should get excited.
Examples:
•    Green Orb
•    Rare boss drops
•    Valuable components
Loot should feel meaningful rather than routine.
________________________________________
Scarcity Is Important
He wants:
•    Items to retain value.
•    Currency to matter.
•    Rare loot to remain exciting.
He specifically dislikes economies where everyone eventually becomes rich.

__13. Gold Sinks__
Current gold sinks include:
Premium
Removes currency from circulation.
Forging
Consumes items and increases scarcity.
Food/Potions
Ongoing expenses.
Interestingly:
Blessed Amulets were removed as a major gold sink because they no longer align with the intended risk model.

__14. Forging Philosophy__
Todd suggested making forging easier.
Ed essentially rejected every idea.
Examples:
No plans to:
•    Reduce break chances.
•    Increase success rates through extra materials.
•    Make forging safer.
His reasoning:
Forging is supposed to destroy items.
The item destruction:
•    Preserves economy.
•    Creates scarcity.
•    Gives value to drops.
He openly admits he has even considered making forging more punishing.

__15. PvP Griefing Fixes__
To address PvP-test griefing:
Several changes have already been made.
Healing Restrictions
Players can only heal others within the same PvP state.
Examples:
PvP players ↔ PvP players
Non-PvP players ↔ Non-PvP players
________________________________________
Find Person Restrictions
The tracking spell now follows the same logic.
This prevents non-PvP characters from assisting PvP participants.

__16. No Second Trait Page__
One of the clearest answers in the interview.
Trait Presets Are Not Coming
No:
•    PvE spec
•    PvP spec
•    One-click swapping
Reasons:
Financial:
•    Encourages resets.
•    Supports premium sales.
Design:
•    Encourages commitment.
•    Builds identity.
•    Increases consequences.
Ed believes players should commit to builds rather than swapping constantly.

__17. Rogue/Mage Class Identity Concerns__
Ed acknowledges a common criticism:
Rogue and Mage overlap too much.
Particularly:
•    Healer builds
•    Spell builds
•    Endgame scaling
However:
He admits this was somewhat intentional.
The inspiration comes from classic Tibia Paladins:
•    Hybrid gameplay
•    Partial caster
•    Partial combat
He plans to monitor feedback before making drastic changes.

__18. What Excites Ed Most__
Perhaps the most revealing section.
Surprisingly:
It isn't a feature.
It isn't a dungeon.
It isn't a boss.
It's Launch Itself
Not the release date.
But seeing:
•    Permanent progression
•    Real loss
•    Real economy
•    Real wars
•    Real rivalries
Tests aren't "real" to him because wipes eventually happen.
He wants to see how players behave when actions permanently matter.

__19. Launch Readiness__
According to Ed:
The game is "pretty close."
Current work includes:
•    Legal agreements
•    Terms of service
•    Account systems
•    Final content implementation
•    Internal testing
He says the last test dramatically clarified what remains to be completed.

__20. Launch Plan__
When launch approaches:
Step 1:
Release launch trailer.
Step 2:
Open account registration roughly one week before launch.
Step 3:
Distribute Patreon rewards.
Step 4:
Launch.
He specifically does NOT want a surprise launch because account creation servers would become overloaded.

__21. Estimated Timeline__
No release date is being provided.
However:
Ed confirmed:
End of the year remains the goal.
But emphasizes:
•    Legal work
•    Testing
•    Real-life events
could all impact timing.

**__*Key Points of Part 1*__**
This conversation reveals several important design pillars behind Apogea:
**Risk Matters**
Death, loss, PvP, dungeon camping, and danger are intentional parts of the experience.
**Discovery Matters**
Secrets, hidden quests, unique items, Blood Moon mechanics, and unexplained world events are central to the game's identity.
**Community Matters**
Ed wants players to:
•    Organize
•    Form guilds
•    Create rivalries
•    Share discoveries
**Convenience Is Often Rejected**
Whenever a system removes tension too effectively, Ed tends to push back against it.
**Apogea Is Being Built as a Passion Project**
More than anything else, Ed repeatedly emphasizes:
"I'm making the game I want to play, not a game where I'm the main character."
That philosophy appears to drive almost every major design choice discussed in this first section.

**__*Key Points of Part 2*__**
The biggest themes in this second half are:
**Scarcity Is Good**
Ed wants money, items, and success to feel valuable.
**Convenience Is Dangerous**
Many requested quality-of-life features are intentionally rejected.
**Consequences Matter**
Death, character choices, PvP decisions, and economic mistakes should all feel meaningful.
**The Economy Comes First**
Many design choices are being evaluated primarily through their effect on item value and long-term market health.
**Apogea Is Nearing Release**
For the first time, Ed sounds less focused on major system changes and more focused on finishing content, legal requirements, testing, and launch preparation.
The strongest overall signal from Part 2 is that Apogea appears to have moved from active experimentation into final preparation mode, with most fundamental systems already decided and only balance, content completion, and testing remaining before launch.
